messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED - streaming-tail-latency surge in us-east - p95 >= 1.8s, p99 >= 9s across SSE/WebSocket paths. Pager: alice (oncall). Link: https://status.redwood.example/incident/7390012345

alice (oncall): seeing the alert. anyone already on it? which services are impacted?

ben (sre): I'm on metrics. p95 for streaming responses (route /v1/stream) jumped from ~200ms -> 1.8s in the last 6m. p99s spike to 9.7s. error rate not large but chunking stalls observed.

ben (sre): Query I ran: 
```
# prometheus
sum(rate(streaming_chunk_delay_seconds_count[5m])) by (region)
```
shows concentrated spikes in region=us-east-1 and backing proxy pool at 90% write queue depth.

carla (platform): also seeing kept-alive sockets accumulating on streaming-proxy hosts prov-proxy-1..3. Kernel TCP recv buffer not full but write buffers huge. Could be slow client consumers causing backpressure.

frank (eng-runtime): stack traces from runtime show long KV-cache lock holds during token-join operations when output chunks are buffered for function calling. Might be blocking streaming flush path.

dan (pager): paging primary oncall for proxy infra cc'ing eng-runtime. marking sev=P1 until mitigated. Notifying oncall rotation.

alice (oncall): plan: 1) throttle slow consumers at proxy (soft drop) 2) disable aggregated chunk batching temporarily 3) route new streams to fallback proxy cluster in us-west while we mitigate us-east 4) notify CS with customer impact.

eva (support): ETA to reach out to customers? We have 3 paying customers hitting >1% request delay threshold. I'll send templated note once we know mitigation.

ben (sre): I'm going to flip proxy keepalive/write-timeout on prov-proxy to shorter (45s -> 15s) to force cleanup of hung clients. Also increase streaming write concurrency from 200 -> 300 for a quick scale. Doing this now via terraform-runbook.

deploy-bot: Started runbook #7390012345-proxy-keepalive-change by ben (sre). See run id: r-8c7f.

carla (platform): rolling keepalive change to prov-proxy pool canary on prov-proxy-3 first. I'm kicking it now.

frank (eng-runtime): disabling chunk aggregation: set ENV STREAM_CHUNK_AGGREGATION=false on runtime-gateway canary. patch: 
```
kubectl set env deployment/runtime-gateway STREAM_CHUNK_AGGREGATION=false -n prod --record
```
This will cause more smaller writes but should reduce lock contention.

alice (oncall): frank, after you flip that, monitor p95/p99 and number of blocked goroutines. Ben, keep an eye on proxy queue depth.

ben (sre): canary applied to prov-proxy-3. Initial metrics: write queue depth dropped 20% in 60s. p95 down to ~1.1s. p99 still high ~6.5s.

frank (eng-runtime): aggregation disabled on 10% runtime pods. goroutine dump shows KV cache lock median hold time reduced 70%. Good signal.

dan (pager): starting traffic steering: send 30% new streams to fallback cluster us-west via smart-router. This should reduce pressure while working on root cause.

ev a (support): (reaction) :thumbsup: - customer comm draft ready, will send once p95 under 500ms for 10m window or we decide to roll back changes.

carla (platform): prov-proxy-3 canary healthy after cfg change. proceeding to roll to prov-proxy-1/2 with staggered 30s waits.

ben (sre): after rolling keepalive change across pool and runtime aggregation disabled cluster-wide: p95 ~380ms, p99 ~1.8s. Streaming stall count dropped to baseline.

alice (oncall): great. are there any lingering client backpressure signals? e.g., slow consumers with small window sizes or TCP half-open?

carla (platform): we still see ~0.5% of clients with very low read bandwidth causing per-connection write queues to back up. We have a long-term plan to implement selective pre-emptive windowing and per-client token bucket. For now throttle/close after 20s of no progress.

frank (eng-runtime): root cause summary so far: chunk aggregation plus a codepath that grabbed KV-cache lock during final chunk flush created head-of-line lock under high concurrent streaming traffic with a subset of slow consumers. That amplified proxy write queue growth -> holistic p95/p99 spike.

ben (sre): mitigation summary: 1) reduce keepalive/write-timeout 2) disable aggregation 3) scale out proxy pool (2 extra instances) 4) steer traffic to fallback cluster. All applied.

alice (oncall): Dan, please take 1hr handoff. I need to step out for 30m. Document actions and timeline so we can include in postmortem.

dan (pager): taking handoff, notes logged in incident runbook. I'll watch p99 for next 60m.

eva (support): Sent customer notices to three impacted accounts: ACME Inc, NovaML, and FlowAnalytics. Message included outage summary, mitigation steps, and ETA for postmortem. Customers acknowledged.

deploy-bot: Runtime config change STREAM_CHUNK_AGGREGATION=false rolled to 100% of pods by frank (eng-runtime).

ben (sre): p95 stable at ~320-400ms for 12 minutes. p99 dropping toward 900-1200ms. No further error rate increase.

frank (eng-runtime): I'm preparing a small patch to move KV-cache ops off the hot path and add per-request non-blocking flush. Will open a PR with tests. Aim: patch + canary tomorrow morning.

carla (platform): we'll schedule proxy-level client slow-consumer mitigation (selective TCP write limit) as medium-priority infra change.

alice (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Severity downgraded to SEV-REC (monitoring + postmortem). Dan continues watch. Please add any remaining action items to runbook. cc: @execs.

dan (pager): watching. will alert if p99 > 2s again.

ben (sre): final note for postmortem: timeline, root cause (aggregation + KV-lock), mitigations applied, customer impact (3 customers < 5 min impact window each, no data loss), follow-ups (runtime patch, proxy slow-consumer control, improve metrics for queue depth per-connection).

frank (eng-runtime): thanks team. opening postmortem draft now.

incident-bot: Incident 7390012345 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem required. Severity: P1 (mitigated).

alice (oncall): handing back to rotation. good job everyone :clap: 

dan (pager): acknowledged, closing this thread when postmortem link available.
